API CONDITION ANSWERED AT THE PINNED SOURCE INTERFACE, RUNTIME STILL UNPROVEN.

At 6edc0f1, the exact call is AMRParser.parse_sentences(batch, batch_size, roberta_batch_size, beam=1, jamr=False, no_isi=False, unicode_normalize=False). Its documented and implemented batch type is List[List[String]] of already-tokenised sentences. We will pass one atlas token-text vector per request and never call AMRParser.tokenize.

The method returns annotations and completed state machines in input order. Each returned machine publicly retains its tokens vector; the bridge envelope will pair the original stable request ID with annotations[i] and machines[i].tokens. Scala requires response count equality, unique/exact request IDs, and returned tokens byte-equal to the requested atlas vector before marker resolution. Any parser truncation or rewriting therefore becomes TokenEchoMismatch. Order is checked again after ID-keying rather than trusted positionally.

This proves the intended API seam exists in source. It does not prove the old Torch/fairseq runtime can execute it; the pinned-runtime spike may still stop on dependency or model loading. Held-out source remains deliberately unnamed until the architecture is dispositioned, but it will be named and independently admitted before the content-addressed runtime freeze, as the amended order requires.
